newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down after quiet session.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down after quiet session.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate reversed an opening gain to close down 10 basis points at 28.15 percent on Monday after an initial bout of speculation subsided, traders said.

"Government rates opened up above real rates, but that was just speculation ahead of the cutoff date (for banks settling outstanding balances on checking accounts held with the central bank)," a trader said.
Banks have to settle accounts with the central bank on Tuesday.
"As there was no great reason for the initial spurt in rates, they soon returned to an average level for recent sessions," a dealer said.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 25 basis points at 29.75 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 4.256 billion pesos to offset liquidity shortfalls by auctioning three credits, which it assigned at rates of between 29.61 and 29.97 percent.
Despite upward pressure on secondary rates during the session, traders expected primary rates to be mixed at the auction, whose results were to be announced later in the day.

A Reuters survey of money market traders showed they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes to be assigned at 27.55 percent, which would be an increase of 28 basis points from last week's rate. Traders forecast marginal falls for other maturities.
"Secondary rates were under pressure, but dealers are most likely to try to hold rates back so any increases will be marginal," a trader said.
Traders said that inflation figures were announced too late to have any immediate impact on trading.
Banco de Mexico announced that inflation for the first half of December was 2.34 percent.
"The figures were greater than expected, but the market had virtually closed and trading was light. Dealers are covered until next year," a trader said.
Total credit maturities estimated for Tuesday were 8.207 billion pesos.
